nodes.label: StoryScope: Investigating idiosyncrasies in AI fiction
nodes.author: Jenna Russell, Rishanth Rajendhran, Chau Minh Pham, Mohit Iyyer, John Wieting
nodes.rationale: Proposes STORYSCOPE pipeline for extracting discourse-level narrative features from fiction to distinguish human-written from AI-generated stories without relying on stylistic signals.

nodes.label: STORYSCOPE Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Three-stage pipeline: (1) structured narrative templates, (2) cross-source comparative analysis, (3) discourse-level feature discovery; yields 304 interpretable narrative features across 10 NarraBench dimensions.

nodes.label: Structured Narrative Templates
nodes.rationale: Intermediate representation converting prose into structured JSON fields organized along 10 narrative dimensions (Agent, Social Network, Event, Plot, Structure, Setting, Time, Revelation, Perspective, Style).

nodes.label: Cross-Source Comparative Analysis
nodes.rationale: Stage that performs pairwise comparisons across sources writing from same prompt; produces structured JSON with per-source dimension notes and cross-source divergences to guide feature discovery.

nodes.label: Narrative Feature Discovery
nodes.rationale: Extracts interpretable narrative features from comparative analyses using 10 specialized expert prompts grounded in NarraBench dimensions; yields 304 features after deduplication via embedding clustering.

nodes.label: Core Narrative Features
nodes.rationale: 30 stable and important features for binary human-vs-AI task with strong consistent separation across all five AI models; examples include thematic explicitness, agency in resolution, narratorial commentary.

nodes.label: Fingerprint Features
nodes.rationale: 75 source-specific features identified from six-way multiclass task; enable fine-grained attribution by capturing unique narrative choices of each AI model and human authors.

nodes.label: STORYSCOPE Parallel Corpus
nodes.rationale: 10,272 human-written stories from Books3 paired with AI-generated mirrors from five LLMs (Claude, DeepSeek, Gemini, GPT, Kimi); 61,608 total stories averaging ~5,000 words each.

nodes.label: AI Detection via Narrative Features
nodes.rationale: Narrative features alone achieve 93.2% macro-F1 for human vs. AI detection, retaining 97% of performance of models with stylistic cues; robust to stylistic editing (93.9% macro-F1 after LAMP rewriting).

nodes.label: Six-Way Authorship Attribution
nodes.rationale: Narrative features achieve 68.4% macro-F1 for six-way attribution; human and Claude most distinctive (88.5% and 77.1% F1 without style), while DeepSeek/Gemini/Kimi form confused cluster.

nodes.label: AI Narrative Characteristics
nodes.rationale: AI stories over-explain themes (77% vs 52% explicit narration), favor tidy single-track plots (79% no subplots vs 57%), convey emotion through bodily sensations (81% vs 38%), avoid specific intertextual references.

nodes.label: Human Narrative Characteristics
nodes.rationale: Human stories subvert linearity with time jumps and flashbacks, frame protagonist choices as morally ambiguous, reference specific texts (47% vs 24%), break fourth wall (67% vs 39%), exhibit greater narrative diversity.

nodes.label: Claude Narrative Fingerprint
nodes.rationale: Claude produces flat event escalation, reverent approach to literary tradition (62%), favors epilogues, avoids dream sequences; most distinctive of five AI models.

nodes.label: GPT Narrative Fingerprint
nodes.rationale: GPT centers on socially-oriented storytelling with gossip/rumor as plot mechanism (64%), frames stories as reflections from years/decades ago, ensemble-heavy social networks, subverts expectations (41%).

nodes.label: Gemini Narrative Fingerprint
nodes.rationale: Gemini produces tidiest endings with extended denouements, bleakest settings (88%), forms confused cluster with DeepSeek and Kimi.

nodes.label: DeepSeek Narrative Fingerprint
nodes.rationale: DeepSeek front-loads crucial context that other sources leave until later; forms confused cluster with Gemini and Kimi.

nodes.label: Kimi Narrative Fingerprint
nodes.rationale: Kimi has fewest fingerprints and lowest F1, sitting at generic center of AI distribution with no distinctive narrative choices.

nodes.label: Narrative Rarity Analysis
nodes.rationale: Human stories have higher mean rarity percentile (0.71 vs 0.49); 24.7% of human stories in top 10% rarest vs 7.1% of AI; human story ranked rarest of six versions 57.8% of time.

nodes.label: Narrative Feature Space Clustering
nodes.rationale: Five AI models occupy tight cluster well-separated from human stories; mean human-AI centroid distance 1.6× mean AI-AI distance; human stories more dispersed (22% greater distance to centroid).

nodes.label: NarraBench Narrative Taxonomy
nodes.rationale: Established taxonomy of 12 narrative dimensions (10 used in STORYSCOPE) grounded in literary theory; provides theoretical foundation for structured narrative representation.

nodes.label: LAMP Span-Level Rewriting Framework
nodes.rationale: Framework identifying and rewriting seven categories of AI writing artifacts; used to test robustness of narrative features to stylistic editing.

nodes.label: STORYSCOPE: Narrative Feature Extraction Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Extracts interpretable narrative features at scale to distinguish human vs. AI-generated stories; achieves 93.2% macro-F1 on binary detection and 68.4% on six-way attribution using 30 core features that capture narrative structure rather than surface stylistic signals.

nodes.label: NarraBench: Narrative Dimension Framework
nodes.rationale: Nine-dimensional narrative analysis framework (Agents, Situatedness, Plot, Perspective, Setting, Social Networks, Events, Revelation, Temporal Structure) organizing 304 interpretable features across five response types (categorical, ordinal, scale, binary, multi-select).

nodes.label: Core AI-Characterizing Features (20)
nodes.rationale: Stable, high-SHAP features that reliably distinguish AI writing: thematic explicitness, embodied emotional expression, causal chain continuity, sensory density, protagonist agency in resolution, and narratorial commentary.

nodes.label: Core Human-Characterizing Features (13)
nodes.rationale: Stable features distinguishing human writing: intertextual strategy diversity, direct reader address, fourth-wall permeability, chronological discontinuity, location variety, and moral ambivalence.

nodes.label: Per-Source Fingerprint Features
nodes.rationale: Model-specific distinguishing features: Human (32 fingerprints), Claude (26), GPT (11), Gemini (11), DeepSeek (7), Kimi (3); enables six-way attribution beyond binary detection.

nodes.label: XGBoost Classifier for Narrative Detection
nodes.rationale: Selected over linear classifiers and random forests for superior performance on both binary and multiclass tasks; integrates with SHAP-based interpretability for feature importance analysis.

nodes.label: Stylometric Baseline (144 features)
nodes.rationale: Surface-level features including sentence/word/paragraph length, vocabulary richness, function-word frequencies, punctuation, dialogue features, readability indices; achieves 85.8% macro-F1 on binary task.

nodes.label: ModernBERT Fine-tuned Baseline
nodes.rationale: Neural baseline fine-tuned on raw story text using same train/val/test split; compared against narrative-only and narrative+style models.

nodes.label: Binoculars Detector
nodes.rationale: External baseline operating on raw text without narrative features; run in accuracy mode with default settings.

nodes.label: Books3 Human-Written Corpus
nodes.rationale: Source of 10,272 human stories (mean 6,403 words); acknowledged copyright issues; used for academic purposes only to understand narrative differences for AI detection and authorship analysis.

nodes.label: AI Models Evaluated (6)
nodes.rationale: Gemini 3 Flash, GPT-5.4, Claude Sonnet 4.6, DeepSeek V3.2, Kimi K2.5; each generated ~10,272 stories with varying adherence to length targets (9.6%-40.2% mean absolute error).

nodes.label: Feature Deduplication via Embedding Clustering
nodes.rationale: Reduced 408 candidate features to 304 using F2LLM-4B embeddings and single-linkage clustering at cosine threshold 0.85; merged 65 multi-feature clusters (25.5% reduction).

nodes.label: Template Extraction via LLM
nodes.source_location: Section B, Are templates truly needed?
nodes.rationale: Intermediate step converting raw stories to structured narrative templates before feature extraction; aspect-based application achieves 95.4% feature coverage vs. 68.4% for single-call approach.

nodes.label: Aspect-Based Feature Application
nodes.source_location: Section C, Why not single shot application?
nodes.rationale: Restricts each LLM call to one NarraBench dimension; achieves 95.4% feature coverage by preserving near-complete coverage across all narrative dimensions.

nodes.label: SHAP-Based Feature Importance Analysis
nodes.rationale: Classifies features as stable-important, unstable-important, stable-weak, or noise; core features require top-quartile SHAP, median stability, 95th-percentile null significance, and cross-model consistency.

nodes.label: Length-Confound Audit
nodes.source_location: Section G, Does length matter for narrative detection?
nodes.rationale: Narrative model achieves 93.2% macro-F1 on both full and length-matched test sets (2,754 stories); demonstrates separation is not driven by human-longer/AI-shorter length contrast.

nodes.label: Memorization-Risk Audit
nodes.source_location: Section F, Memorization risk in story generation
nodes.rationale: Flags 0.70% of generated stories as high-risk via 13-gram and 8-gram overlap detection; removing high-risk prompts (1.67%) leaves detectability conclusions essentially unchanged.

nodes.label: Per-Story Narrative Rarity Analysis
nodes.rationale: Computes mean Euclidean distance to k=25 nearest neighbors in narrative space; human stories shifted toward higher rarity (mean percentile 0.71 vs. 0.49 for AI, Cohen's d=0.83).

nodes.label: Topic-Wise Detection Performance Analysis
nodes.source_location: Section G, Does topic matter for detection?
nodes.rationale: Categorized stories into 12 BISAC topics; binary macro-F1 ranges 90.0%-96.2%, six-way 65.8%-70.8%; Kruskal-Wallis test finds no significant topic-wise differences (H=4.69, p=0.46).

nodes.label: Human Validation Study
nodes.source_location: Section C, Human validation against annotators
nodes.rationale: Two annotators on 240 story-feature items; model-annotator Cohen's κ = 0.84 (mean), human-human κ = 0.74; demonstrates model reliability comparable to human agreement.

nodes.label: Gemini 3 Flash Feature Extractor Reliability
nodes.rationale: Repeated-measures design with 300 outputs; Krippendorff's α=0.90, mean pairwise Cohen's κ=0.89; minimal thinking variant chosen for cost efficiency with minimal performance trade-off.
